batch_file.activation: One-time Ed25519 activation commitment on chain (affine2|activate|<hotkey>|<sig>), unchanged: python -m subnet.register --wallet W --hotkey H --execute from https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine. It proves the hotkey can open the sealed link.
batch_file.cap: Live cap: mining.json training.batch_cap (max_tasks_per_miner prompts, max_rollouts_per_miner rollouts; now 250 x 8 = 2,000 rollouts). The validator can change it at any time; the value read at your turn applies.

batch_file.fresh_turns: Jacob 2026-10-30: the 10 hotkeys whose turn since the held-out gate went live (E271+) was RED with 0 < weighted_z <= 1.00 each get ONE fresh turn ahead of the line, oldest first, under these batch-file rules. It is used only by a real turn: a missing or invalid file is a skip and the grant stays open. List: training.k1.queue_grants.

kit.about: Miner kit: the live trainer (v8.3.4 / host-v834c host + engine; train.kl accepted but ignored), batch checker (ff_format), held-out gate (heldout.py, gate_core.py, gate_service.py), probe sampling + grader, the 7,496-task affine_math file, the 21,574-task public gate pool (data/gate-pool-v2.jsonl) and exact pins, verbatim (validator/MANIFEST.sha256), plus tools: fetch_head.py, generate.py, make_batch.py, check_batch.py, train_step.py (one live step locally), gate_eval.py (the gate procedure and math), simulate_turn.sh, tests/test_kit_cpu.py.

link.contains: object_key, put_url, put_headers, get_url, issued_at, expires_at
link.opens_with: libsodium crypto_box_seal_open with your hotkey's Ed25519 seed converted to X25519 (PyNaCl: SealedBox(SigningKey(seed).to_curve25519_private_key()).decrypt(base64 sealed))
link.reissued: every 30 minutes with fresh presigned URLs for the same object, each valid 24 hours
link.who: every registered SN120 hotkey (UID != 0) with the Ed25519 activation commitment that has not had its turn yet

batch_file.model: Generate against the published head (mining.json checkpoint). Head files: current_url (signed current.json -> manifest_url -> opening.json payload.checkpoint files + read_urls; checkpoint id = sha256 of the canonical JSON {file: sha256}); miner kit: kit/fetch_head.py downloads and verifies them. fp32 master manifest: https://affine.io/k1/fp32-master/<head>.json.
batch_file.object: One private object per hotkey: private/ff/v1/miners/<hotkey>/batch.json. Overwrite it any time. What is there when your turn comes is what is trained.
batch_file.privacy: Your file is private until your turn is decided GREEN; then the exact file is published at https://affine.io/k1/turns/<epoch>/batch.json. RED files stay private.
batch_file.publish: Only GREEN turns are published: the head (bf16 + fp32 master), turn.json and the exact batch file. RED: decision, counts and the file sha256 only.
batch_file.queue: One turn per hotkey and per registration (UID + registration block), permanently, pass or fail. Base order: registration block, then UID; UID 0 excluded; served hotkeys and registrations leave the line. Squat-trim (Jacob 2026-11-05): expected wait = max(1 day, N_ahead / turn_rate) with N_ahead = unserved registrations ahead in registration-block order and turn_rate = turns/day over the last 24h; a registration with no present+valid batch file whose age exceeds 2x that expected wait is moved to the back of the queue (keeps eligibility; ordered among demoted keys by registration block). Any key with a valid file is never demoted. Preview of the next 8: training.k1.queue_next (also https://affine.io/k1.json, which publishes expected_wait, deadline and expired_back_of_queue).
batch_file.reference_script: https://affine.io/ff/affine_batch.py (Python standard library only; link, check, upload, download, status). It is a helper, not a mining client.
rules: UTF-8 JSON, at most 160 MiB, exactly the keys shown (v1: version, hotkey, groups; v2: the same plus the optional train). Prompts non-empty and distinct; at least one rollout per prompt, any number per prompt.

reward: any finite number, used exactly as given. Within a prompt the advantage is reward minus the mean reward of that prompt's rollouts (a prompt with one rollout: the reward itself); the overlong penalty in training.loss still applies.

prompt: plain text. It is rendered as one user message with the model's chat template and the generation prompt: tokenizer.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], add_generation_prompt=True) with the head's tokenizer.
output: the assistant text after that prompt (include the <think>...</think> part if you want it trained). Tokenized with tokenizer.encode(output, add_special_tokens=False).
<|im_start|>, <|im_end|> and <|endoftext|> must not appear in a prompt or an output.

EOS: an output of up to 32767 tokens gets <|im_end|> appended (it ended). Exactly 32768 tokens = cut at the length cap (no EOS, treated as unresolved/capped). More than 32768 tokens is invalid. Prompt + output must be at most 36864 tokens. Generate with max_tokens 32768 (caps.json, https://affine.io/caps.json: generation, batch files, training and the gate).

Cap: at most training.batch_cap.max_tasks_per_miner prompts and training.batch_cap.max_rollouts_per_miner rollouts (live value, tunable). Prompts beyond either cap are dropped whole, in file order; everything kept must be valid.

train (v2 only): lr in [1.25e-7, 1e-6] (default 5e-7), kl in [0.005, 0.1] (default 0.02), step_mult integer: 1, 2 (default 1), and the knobs in batch_file.train.fields (each with its range and default); all optional; out of range or not a number = invalid file (batch_file.train).
Any rule broken in the kept part makes the whole file invalid: you are skipped for that turn (not charged, you keep your place).

schema.groups: list of {"prompt": string, "rollouts": list of {"output": string, "reward": number}}
schema.hotkey: your ss58 hotkey (must match the object owner)
schema.train: v2 only, optional: {"lr": number, "kl": number, "step_mult": integer, plus any of the knobs in batch_file.train.fields}, all optional. Omitted field = default (= today's trainer). Not allowed in a v1 file.

batch_file.skip: At each turn the queue is walked in order. A member whose file is missing or invalid at that moment is skipped: not charged, keeps its place, and the next member is tried in the same epoch.
batch_file.status: https://affine.io/ff/status.json: the validator's format check of each stored file within about a minute of upload (valid, reason, format, prompts, rollouts; never content or train values)
steps: 1. Have a registered SN120 hotkey (UID != 0) with the one-time Ed25519 activation (batch_file.activation).

2. Write your file in the affine-batch-v1 format (batch_file.schema, batch_file.example, batch_file.rules), or affine-batch-v2 to also set lr / kl / step_mult / the knobs (batch_file.train, batch_file.example_v2): plain-text prompts, each with your rollouts (output text + reward).
3. Check it locally: python3 affine_batch.py check --hotkey <ss58> batch.json (https://affine.io/ff/affine_batch.py, Python standard library only).

4. Get your link: GET https://affine.io/ff/links/<hotkey>.json and open the sealed field with your hotkey seed (batch_file.link.opens_with), or run python3 affine_batch.py link --hotkey <ss58> --key <seed file>.
5. Upload: HTTP PUT the file bytes to put_url with Content-Type: application/octet-stream, or python3 affine_batch.py upload --hotkey <ss58> --key <seed file> batch.json. Overwrite it any time.
6. Within about a minute check https://affine.io/ff/status.json (or python3 affine_batch.py status --hotkey <ss58>): valid true, or the reason it is invalid.
7. Watch the queue preview (training.k1.queue_next, the next 8). At your turn the stored file is copied and trained; the gate decides GREEN or RED.

train.bounds: inclusive. A value outside its range, a non-number (string, bool, null) where a number is expected, a step_mult that is not an integer (2.0, "2", true), a string that is not one of the listed choices, or any other key under "train" makes the whole file invalid: you are skipped for that turn (not charged, you keep your place). Values are never clamped.
train.defaults_rule: Every field is optional and defaults to today's trainer; a file without them, or with every one at its default, trains bit-identically to before (checked on a real GREEN file). Bounds are inclusive; out of range, the wrong type, an unknown choice or an unknown key makes the whole file invalid (never clamped).

adam_eps.meaning: eps in the normalized-gradient term g / (abs(g) + eps); larger eps shrinks the per-tensor step of tensors with small gradients (the step direction stays g / norm(g))

adv_center.meaning: advantage of a rollout: mean = reward - mean reward of its prompt group (today); none = the raw reward; group_norm = (reward - mean) / (std + 1e-6) within the group

adv_clip.default_meaning: omitted = no clip (null is not accepted)
adv_clip.meaning: if set, advantages are clipped to [-adv_clip, +adv_clip] after centering; omit it for no clip (today)

clamp_mode.meaning: per_tensor: each tensor's step is capped at c_t = 2e-5 x norm(W_t) (today). global_norm: no per-tensor cap; the whole step is scaled down to global_norm_cap if larger. both: per-tensor cap, then the global cap at global_norm_cap

global_norm_cap.meaning: the global step-norm cap used by clamp_mode global_norm / both (ignored with per_tensor, which keeps the fixed cap 1.0)

kl.meaning: accepted but ignored as of trainer v8.3.4 (2026-11-05): still parsed in [0.005,0.1] so miner files validate; kl_applied=0, no Genesis ref

loss_agg.meaning: seq_mean: every rollout weighs the same (mean over its tokens, then over rollouts; today). token_mean: every token weighs the same (long rollouts weigh more)

lr.meaning: step size of the one training step (see math)

lr_scale_attn.meaning: multiplies the step of every attention tensor (self_attn.*, linear_attn.*); 0 freezes them

lr_scale_early.meaning: multiplies the step of every tensor in decoder layers 0..15 (on top of the group scale); 0 freezes them

lr_scale_embed.meaning: multiplies the step of embed_tokens; 0 freezes it

lr_scale_late.meaning: multiplies the step of every tensor in decoder layers 16..31 (on top of the group scale); 0 freezes them

lr_scale_lm_head.meaning: multiplies the step of lm_head; 0 freezes it

lr_scale_mlp.meaning: multiplies the step of every mlp.* tensor; 0 freezes them

step_mult.meaning: step multiplier k (proposed in #120 by duongna): the whole per-tensor step is multiplied by k, i.e. lr and the per-tensor cap c_t are scaled together. Still one gradient and one step from the head, so no extra trainer time. k = 1 is the previous step exactly.

weight_decay.meaning: decoupled weight decay inside the per-tensor step norm (2-D non-bias tensors); it changes step sizes, not the direction

train.math: m = lr / 5e-7. Per tensor t (fp32 master W_t): d_t = 5e-7 * (g_t / (|g_t| + 1e-8) + 0.01 * W_t * [W_t >= 2-D and not a bias]); c_t = 2e-5 * (1 - 1e-6) * ||W_t||; n0_t = min(||d_t||, c_t) (the default-lr step norm); n_t = min(m * n0_t, c_t); s = min(1, 1.0 / ||n||) over all tensors; W_t_new = W_t - s * n_t * g_t / ||g_t||. lr below the default shrinks every tensor's step by exactly m; lr above the default only grows tensors that are under the per-tensor cap c_t, up to it (the cap is a hard ceiling; many tensors already sit at it with the default). The default (and any v1 file) is exactly the previous step. kl replaces kl_coefficient in L = loss_scale * (1/N) * sum_i (1/K_i) * sum_t [pg + kl * k3] for that turn. step_mult k (trainer v8.3.3k/l): n_t is multiplied by k before the global cap, n_t(k) = k * n_t, so a tensor at the per-tensor cap moves k * c_t (the cap scales with k); s = min(1, 1.0 / ||n(k)||) is unchanged (the default step norm is about 0.023). k = 1 is exactly the previous step. Knobs (trainer v8.3.3l): e_t = lr * (g/(|g| + adam_eps) + weight_decay * W [2-D, not bias]); a_t = group scale (lr_scale_attn / mlp / embed / lm_head, other tensors 1) x lr_scale_early (layers 0..15) or lr_scale_late (16..31); per_tensor / both: n_t = k * min(m * a_t * min(||e_t||, c_t), c_t); global_norm: n_t = k * m * a_t * ||e_t||; G = 1.0 (per_tensor) or min(1.0, global_norm_cap); s = min(1, G / ||n||); Delta_t = s * n_t * g_t / ||g_t||. Loss: adv_center / adv_clip set the GRPO advantage; loss_agg token_mean weighs every token equally instead of every rollout. With every knob at its default the v8.3.3j/k code path runs unchanged.
train.published: The effective lr, kl, step_mult and knobs of a turn are published with the turn only if it is GREEN (k1/turns/<epoch>/turn.json training.train_params, mining.json training.miner_train_params.recent_green_turns). RED: private like the file.
train.unchanged: Everything else is fixed by the validator: per-tensor cap and global norm cap (except through step_mult / the knobs), gradient clip, overlong penalty, starting head, one step per turn, batch cap, queue and gate.

batch_file.turn: Queue unchanged (training.k1): one turn per hotkey and per registration. At your turn the validator copies your object (kept as evidence), checks the format, takes one GRPO step from the published head with your rewards and runs the promotion gate. GREEN: promoted, you earn. RED: discarded.
batch_file.upload: HTTP PUT the file bytes to put_url with the header Content-Type: application/octet-stream. Read back with get_url.

notice: Upload ONE batch file (prompts, your rollouts, your rewards) to your private per-hotkey object; at your turn it is copied, format-checked and trained. See batch_file. New (2026-10-31): an affine-batch-v2 file may set the turn's lr and kl (batch_file.train). New (2026-11-02, trainer v8.3.3l): optional train fields step_mult (integer: 1, 2) and lr_scale_attn, lr_scale_mlp, lr_scale_embed, lr_scale_lm_head, lr_scale_early, lr_scale_late, adam_eps, weight_decay, clamp_mode, global_norm_cap, loss_agg, adv_center, adv_clip. All default to today's trainer, so a file without them trains exactly as before (batch_file.train.fields). Training/generation/batch files use 32,768 output tokens (https://affine.io/caps.json); generate with max_tokens 32,768. The promotion gate stays at 65,536 output tokens (see llms.txt). New (2026-11-05): the public gate pool is gate-pool-v2 (21,574 tasks = gate-pool-v1 + 2,269 harder hard-v1 problems; miner/data/gate-pool-v2.jsonl, llms.txt section 5) from the first round on the next new head after epoch 767.
protocol: free-file affine-batch-v1 / affine-batch-v2 (v2 from 2026-10-31: optional per-turn lr and kl; from 2026-11-02 also step_mult and the optional optimizer / loss knobs)
